placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the south face of blk_south_water_dearborn, the block's Lake Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its east wall is fixed by the west wall of recon_1835_blk_south_water_dearborn_d5_08, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at Lake Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 4.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

frontage.why: T-0432, the fourth and last of the South Water blocks T-0420 was split into, and the first roofs this programme has built on the reach since the ruling of 2026-08-29 discharged the refusal that held it. THE REFUSAL AND WHAT DISCHARGED IT: T-0143 and T-0188 each declined to tighten a party-line row against a street line that might still move, and T-0317 inherited the decline; T-0009 closed it — the drawn South Water line does NOT move, the corridor was re-derived from committed control (`recentred`, +8.58 m) and data/streets/1835.json was not touched. This run does not stand on that corridor in any case: it stands on the block's LAKE face, which is committed geometry derived from the street centrelines exactly as the north face is, and the distinction T-0143 and T-0188 were protecting — a row on the BLOCK FACE rather than on a re-derived line — survives the ruling unchanged and is what this run is built on. THE FACE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, by the command T-A14 made of it — tools/measure_street_frontage.py south_water lake dearborn state — and on the committed dataset Lake carries 17 documented records and 8 inferred households within 25 m of its centreline against South Water's 15 and 2, Dearborn's 6 and 1 and State's 3 and 0. That reading does not have to be re-fought against the first deal's, because THE NORTH FACE IS FULL: lots 0, 2, 4 and 6 all carry a roof — the Chicago American's office, Frederick Thomas's shop, the first deal's three-unit run and the Chappel infant school — so the only frontage this block has left is on Lake, and both readings of the business face send this run to the same place. WHAT BINDS IS THE STANDARD'S THIRD CLAUSE. Lot 7 is the block's one free CORNER lot, the south-east one, fronting Lake Street along its long edge and State Street along its short one, and a corner lot BUILDS TO THE CORNER — a west-anchored run packs back toward the middle of the face and stops wherever its roofs run out, so the corner is the one piece of frontage a row can never reach. The run is packed EAST to it. AND THE GRADING RUNS THE OTHER WAY, which is the same separation T-0317 first demonstrated at Market: the corner clause fixes WHERE THE ROW STANDS and the end rule fixes WHICH ROOF STANDS WHERE IN IT. This corner is at State Street, the platted town's eastern limit with the fort's reservation beyond it, and it is the far end of the face from the Dearborn Street drawbridge, the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835. THE END RULE IS READ, NOT ASSERTED: tools/measure_end_rule.py reads this south face at a spread of 77.76 m and a unit step of 6.07 m under the walked criterion and grades on it, while the same face under T-A11's straight line reads a 1.84 m unit step and is BELOW THE FLOOR — so the walk is what makes a grading possible here at all, and the straight line would have been grading this parcel's own declared setback invention. Walked, lot 1 stands 158.44 m from the bridge, lot 3 184.36 m, lot 5 210.28 m and lot 7 236.20 m. The row is therefore graded WEST, toward the bridge: the meanest of the three dwellings takes the corner and the best closes the run at the west end. WHICH OF THE THREE IS THE MEANEST IS THE ONE THING THIS PARCEL COULD NOT READ OFF A SINGLE CRITERION, and the arrangement note holds the reasoning and the measurement. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the lot's own stretch of it and the end the run packs toward are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. The Lake face carries no committed street wall for the run to adopt — the two roofs already standing on that tier, the first deal's cottage on lot 3 and its log dwelling on lot 5, are one-per-lot placements set back inside their own lots at 6.0 m and 5.5 m — so this run is the first line on the face and states the margin rather than adopting one.
